title: Customer fingerprint emulator for VPC/on-prem benchmarking
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We need a reliable way to reproduce customer traffic characteristics inside Private/VPC/on-prem environments for deterministic performance benchmarking. Existing 'replay' runners exercise request streams but lack a compact representation of customer fingerprint (client mix, KV cache warmup patterns, sequence-length distribution, burstiness) that is both portable across clusters and parameterizable for synthetic experiments. This ticket scopes a lightweight 'Customer Fingerprint Emulator' (CFE) that captures and reproduces the statistical and operational properties of a customer's load for tokens/sec and latency SLO profiling, p95 tracking, and automated regression detection in private deployments.
proposed_solution: Build a modular emulator that: 1) ingests anonymized traces (prefix lengths, per-request token counts, model variant, cache hit indicators); 2) generates workload profiles (sequence-length histogram, concurrency mix, burst intervals); 3) runs in a containerized harness that can be deployed inside customer VPCs or on-prem infra to replay workload deterministically with configurable randomness seeds; 4) emits telemetry compatible with our existing Console ingestion (tokens/sec, p95, p50, error rate) and regression hooks for automated alerts.
implementation_steps: 1) Trace schema: finalize schema for anonymized customer fingerprint (fields, sampling rate, retention) and add export tool to existing repro harnesses.
2) Emulator engine: implement generator that produces request streams from fingerprint (supports deterministic seed and adjustable variance parameters).
3) Container harness: build Kubernetes helm chart + on-prem systemd package to deploy emulator paired with our runtime agent and local metrics sink.
4) Telemetry adapter: implement Prometheus + Console exporter for tokens/sec and latency percentiles with tags for model variant and cache/hot-kv state.
5) Regression pipeline: integrate outputs with existing regression detection (baseline capture, diff thresholds for tokens/sec and p95, automatic regression alerts in Console).
6) End-to-end tests: author deterministic scenarios using small language model images to validate reproducibility and bit-for-bit metrics across runs.
7) Documentation & runbook: public runbook for SEs to deploy emulator into customer VPCs and interpret results.
acceptance_criteria: The emulator ingests a fingerprint file and produces a replay stream that reproduces tokens/sec within 5% median error compared to original trace over 30-minute runs.
p95 latency reported by Console for the emulator-run matches offline replay within 10% for at least 90% of test scenarios.
Deterministic replay: given the same fingerprint and seed, two runs produce metrics with <2% variance for tokens/sec and <5% variance for p95.
Emulator runs inside customer VPC/on-prem with provided helm chart or package and does not require outbound egress except optional metrics ingestion endpoints.
Regression detection rules trigger on sustained deviations (tokens/sec drop >15% or p95 increase >20%) and create a Console incident with attached artifacts.
Security review completed for trace ingestion/export and anonymization process.
test_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint parser/generator with synthetic traces.
Deterministic E2E test using lightweight model image across two different clusters to assert reproducibility.
Load soak: 4-hour run to validate stability and memory/CPU profiles under sustained load.
Regression test harness that runs nightly against a baseline fingerprint and reports diffs to Console.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal infra only (SE lab) for 2 weeks. Beta: select enterprise customers with SE assistance and opt-in telemetry for 4 weeks. GA: public helm chart + on-prem package, default integration with Dedicated and Private onboarding. Provide optional managed run support for first 3 enterprise customers.
risks: Sensitive data leakage if fingerprints are not properly anonymized — mitigated by schema that strips PII and an enforced local-only export mode.
Emulator may under/over-estimate KV cache warmup effects vs real customer runtime — will iterate by introducing warmup phase modeling and cache priming features.
Resource usage in small on-prem installs could cause noisy neighbor effects — add configurable rate caps and local resource reservations.
